# v1.1.0-dev.100: The highest refresh rate, and starting with Windows

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.99`.

One fix and one new setting.

## "Highest this size offers" now sets the highest

The refresh-rate dropdown's first option named the highest rate and did
not set it. A 2560x1440 panel sitting at 60 Hz with 144 on offer stayed
at 60, and the apply reported success.

That option means "no particular rate", which is deliberate. It is what
lets one profile ask for the best rate on whatever display it lands on,
so the answer has to be worked out at the display rather than baked into
the saved profile. The cost was that the check which skips a display
already in the right mode ignores a rate nobody named. It answered
"already there" for every display that was the right size, and the
option only ever did anything on a display that was changing size as
well.

The request is now resolved against that display's own mode list first,
and the comparison is against *that*. "The highest" means the highest.

Worth knowing on the first load after you update: profiles that saved a
resolution without naming a rate really will change one now. A screen
can blank for a moment on a display you thought nothing was happening
to. It settles after that, because the next load finds it already there.

## WLM can start with Windows

Settings has a new **Startup** section, at the top of the tab now called
**Startup & Window**.

Tick **Start Window Layout Manager when I sign in to Windows** and it
does. It starts in the tray, which is where WLM lives anyway, so nothing
opens over whatever you signed in to do. If you would rather see the
window, there is a second box under the first for that. Both are off
until you turn them on.

WLM ships as a portable zip with no installer, so it writes its own
startup entry, for the folder you are running from, under your own user
account. Nothing elevated, nothing machine-wide. Move the folder and it
re-points itself the next time you run it. Install an update and it
follows that too.

Two things it will not do. It does not argue with Windows: if you switch
the entry off under Task Manager's Startup tab, that sticks, and the
panel tells you it happened rather than quietly writing over you. And it
cannot clean up after a folder you delete, because a portable app has no
uninstaller to run. Clear the box before you delete the folder, or
Windows keeps reaching for an exe that is gone.

## Smaller things

When Windows turns a mode change down, the message now names the refresh
rate if the rate is what changed. It used to print the width and height,
which on a rate-only change is the one part that was already right.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
